work_mekhilta.composer: School of Rabbi Yishmael; edited by later sages

work_mishnah.rank_desc: The foundation of the Oral Law
work_mishnah.composer: Rabbi Judah ha-Nasi (traditional editor); tannaitic sages

work_yerushalmi_zeraim.rank_desc: A major part of the Palestinian Talmud

work_yerushalmi_moed.rank_desc: A major part of the Palestinian Talmud

work_yerushalmi_nashim.rank_desc: A major part of the Palestinian Talmud

work_yerushalmi_nezikin.rank_desc: A major part of the Palestinian Talmud

work_halakhot_gedolot.composer: Attributed to Simeon Kayyara; authorship debated

work_shiur_qomah.composer: Anonymous; traditionally linked to Rabbi Ishmael

prose.name: The Torah
prose.desc: The Five Books of Moses, read aloud in the synagogue week by week.
prose.detail: Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers and Deuteronomy: the heart of Scripture for every Jewish tradition. A community keeps its scroll in the ark for public reading and its bound copies for study, and a reader returns to them all his life.
prose.study: You open the Torah again and read the week's portion slowly, word by word.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered The Torah at the yeshiva.

prose.name: Nevi'im
prose.desc: The Prophets, from Joshua to Malachi, read in the synagogue as the haftarah.
prose.detail: The Former Prophets tell Israel's story from the conquest of the land to the exile. The Latter Prophets carry the rebukes and consolations of Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel and the Twelve.
prose.study: You take up the Prophets and read their warnings beside their comfort.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Nevi'im at the yeshiva.

work_tanakh_ketuvim.composer: David, Solomon and the sages of Israel, by tradition

prose.name: Ketuvim
prose.desc: The Writings: Psalms, Proverbs, Job, the five scrolls, Daniel, Ezra-Nehemiah and Chronicles.
prose.detail: Songs and wisdom, the scrolls read on the festivals, and the last histories of the biblical canon. The Psalms above all are a book every Jew carries in memory.
prose.study: You read the Writings, from the Psalms to the last pages of Chronicles.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Ketuvim at the yeshiva.

work_tosefta.rank_desc: A tannaitic companion to the Mishnah
work_tosefta.composer: Tannaitic teachings collected after the Mishnah

prose.name: Tosefta
prose.desc: A companion to the Mishnah, gathering tannaitic teachings it left out.
prose.detail: Arranged by the Mishnah's own orders and tractates, the Tosefta keeps rulings, disputes and stories of the same sages. The Talmuds cite such teachings as baraitot.
prose.study: You read the Tosefta beside the Mishnah, tractate by tractate.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Tosefta at the yeshiva.

prose.name: Seder Rav Amram
prose.desc: The first full order of Jewish prayer, sent by the Gaon of Sura to the Jews of Spain.
prose.detail: Answering a request from Spain, Amram Gaon set out the prayers of the year with the laws that govern them. Copies spread through the West, and later prayer books grew out of it.
prose.study: You work through Seder Rav Amram, prayer by prayer and law by law.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Seder Rav Amram at the yeshiva.

work_iggeret_rav_sherira.rank_desc: A geonic history of the tradition

prose.name: Iggeret Rav Sherira Gaon
prose.desc: A gaon's answer to Kairouan on how the Mishnah and the Talmud came to be written.
prose.detail: Asked by the community of Kairouan how the oral teaching was set down, Sherira Gaon traced the chain of sages from the Mishnah through the savoraim to the geonim of his own day. It became the standard account of the rabbinic tradition.
prose.study: You follow Sherira Gaon's letter down the generations of the sages.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Iggeret Rav Sherira Gaon at the yeshiva.

work_rabbenu_hananel.rank_desc: A North African commentary on the Talmud

prose.name: Commentary of Rabbenu Hananel
prose.desc: A Kairouan commentary that sums up the Talmud's discussion and rules on it.
prose.detail: Rabbenu Hananel explained the Bavli's argument briefly, drew on the Yerushalmi and the geonim, and stated the law. His work carried geonic learning across North Africa and beyond.
prose.study: You read Rabbenu Hananel's summaries against the Talmud's own long argument.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Commentary of Rabbenu Hananel at the yeshiva.

prose.name: Mekor Hayyim
prose.desc: Ibn Gabirol's dialogue on matter, form and the divine will, written in Arabic.
prose.detail: A Neoplatonic work that almost never quotes Scripture. Jewish readers largely neglected it, while its Latin translation, Fons Vitae, circulated among Christian scholars who did not know its author was a Jew.
prose.study: You follow Ibn Gabirol's argument from matter and form up to the divine will.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Mekor Hayyim at the yeshiva.

prose.name: Sefer ha-Mitzvot of Anan
prose.desc: The Aramaic legal code of Anan ben David, honoured by Karaites as a founder.
prose.detail: Anan derived the commandments from Scripture by his own reasoning, often more strictly than the rabbis did. Later Karaites revered him as a founder while departing from many of his rulings.
prose.study: You weigh Anan's rulings against the verses he derived them from.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Sefer ha-Mitzvot of Anan at the yeshiva.

prose.name: Kitab al-Anwar
prose.desc: Qirqisani's Book of Lights and Watchtowers, a Karaite code of law in Arabic.
prose.detail: It opens with a history of the Jewish sects and a defence of deriving law from Scripture by reason and analogy, and then sets out the commandments one by one.
prose.study: You read Qirqisani's arguments and test each against the verse.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Kitab al-Anwar at the yeshiva.

work_yefet_commentary.rank_desc: A Karaite commentary on the whole Bible

prose.name: Commentary of Yefet ben Eli
prose.desc: An Arabic translation of and commentary on the whole Bible by a Jerusalem Karaite.
prose.detail: Yefet, one of the Mourners of Zion, glossed every book of the Bible with close attention to grammar and the plain sense. Karaites made it their standard commentary, and Rabbanite readers such as Abraham ibn Ezra read it and argued with it.
prose.study: You read a book of the Bible with Yefet's translation and notes beside it.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Commentary of Yefet ben Eli at the yeshiva.

work_rashi_torah.rank_desc: A work written in this campaign

prose.name: Rashi on the Torah
prose.desc: A commentary on the Torah that explains the plain sense in few words, drawing on midrash where the plain sense needs it.
prose.detail: Written for a reader who knows Hebrew but not every tradition, it answers the questions a careful reader asks of each verse, often in a single line, and sometimes glosses a word in the vernacular.
prose.study: You read the Torah with the commentary at your elbow, verse by verse.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Rashi on the Torah at the yeshiva.

work_rashi_talmud.rank_desc: A work written in this campaign

prose.name: Rashi on the Talmud
prose.desc: A running commentary that lets a student follow the Talmud's argument line by line.
prose.detail: It supplies the missing step, the meaning of a rare word and the point of a question, so that the page can be learned without a teacher at every turn.
prose.study: You learn a tractate with the running commentary beside the page.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Rashi on the Talmud at the yeshiva.

work_hilkhot_harif.rank_desc: A work written in this campaign

prose.name: Halakhot of the Rif
prose.desc: An abridged Talmud that keeps only the passages bearing on practice and states the law.
prose.detail: It follows the order of the Talmud's own tractates, sets aside the long debates and the agadah, and closes each question with the ruling.
prose.study: You read the Rif's halakhot and check each ruling against its sugya.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Halakhot of the Rif at the yeshiva.

work_mishneh_torah.rank_desc: A work written in this campaign

prose.name: Mishneh Torah
prose.desc: A complete code of Jewish law in clear Hebrew, in fourteen books, without the debates or their sources.
prose.detail: Its author meant a reader to need no other book after the Torah. Its order and clarity won it readers everywhere, and its silence about sources drew sharp critics.
prose.study: You work through a book of the Mishneh Torah, law by law.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Mishneh Torah at the yeshiva.

work_moreh_nevukhim.rank_desc: A work written in this campaign

prose.name: Moreh Nevukhim
prose.desc: The Guide of the Perplexed, written in Arabic for a student torn between philosophy and the Torah.
prose.detail: It reads Scripture's bodily language about God as figurative and argues for a God beyond every attribute. Its admirers saw the summit of Jewish thought, its opponents a danger to faith.
prose.study: You read a chapter of the Guide and turn its argument over slowly.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Moreh Nevukhim at the yeshiva.

work_sefer_habahir.rank_desc: A work written in this campaign
work_sefer_habahir.composer: Attributed to Rabbi Nehunya ben ha-Kanah

prose.name: Sefer ha-Bahir
prose.desc: A short, cryptic book on the divine powers and the letters, which surfaced in Provence.
prose.detail: In brief sayings and parables it speaks of ten powers within God. It is among the first books of the Kabbalah.
prose.study: You read the Bahir's parables and try to hold their hidden meaning.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Sefer ha-Bahir at the yeshiva.

work_sefer_hasidim.rank_desc: A work written in this campaign

prose.name: Sefer Hasidim
prose.desc: The book of the German pietists: on fear of Heaven, penitence and conduct in daily life.
prose.detail: Through hundreds of short cases it asks more of a pious man than the law requires, in prayer, in business and with his neighbours, Jewish and Christian.
prose.study: You read the pietists' cases and measure your own conduct against them.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Sefer Hasidim at the yeshiva.

work_tosafot.rank_desc: A work written in this campaign

prose.name: Tosafot
prose.desc: Glosses on the Talmud from the schools of northern France, set against Rashi's commentary.
prose.detail: Comparing distant passages, the Tosafists raise contradictions and resolve them by fine distinctions. They taught generations to read the whole Talmud as one argument.
prose.study: You learn a page with the Tosafot and follow them from one tractate into another.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Tosafot at the yeshiva.

work_zohar.rank_desc: A work written in this campaign
work_zohar.composer: Attributed to Rabbi Shimon bar Yohai

prose.name: Zohar
prose.desc: A vast mystical commentary on the Torah in Aramaic, presented as the teaching of Rabbi Shimon bar Yohai.
prose.detail: It reads the Torah as a map of the divine life and of the soul. It appeared in Castile and grew in authority until many held it holy.
prose.study: You read a passage of the Zohar and try to follow where it leads.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Zohar at the yeshiva.

work_sifra.rank_desc: A tannaitic legal midrash on Leviticus
work_sifra.composer: Tannaitic school of Rabbi Akiva; edited by later sages

prose.name: Sifra (Torat Kohanim)
prose.desc: The tannaitic legal midrash on Leviticus.
prose.detail: The Sifra reads Leviticus line by line to derive the laws of sacrifice, purity and priesthood. It preserves the methods and disputes of the early rabbis, though its final form was shaped by later editors.
prose.study: You trace a law of Leviticus through the Sifra's tightly argued exposition.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Sifra at the yeshiva.

work_sifre_numbers.rank_desc: A tannaitic legal midrash on Numbers
work_sifre_numbers.composer: Tannaitic schools of Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Akiva; edited later

prose.name: Sifre Numbers
prose.desc: A tannaitic legal and homiletic midrash on Numbers.
prose.detail: Sifre Numbers preserves teachings from more than one school of early rabbis. Its laws and narratives follow the wilderness book into questions of vows, offerings, camp order and communal authority.
prose.study: You compare the Sifre's legal readings with the verses of Numbers.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Sifre Numbers at the yeshiva.

work_sifre_deuteronomy.rank_desc: A tannaitic legal midrash on Deuteronomy
work_sifre_deuteronomy.composer: Tannaitic schools of Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Yishmael; edited later

prose.name: Sifre Deuteronomy
prose.desc: A tannaitic legal and homiletic midrash on Deuteronomy.
prose.detail: The Sifre turns Moses' last speeches into a field of legal argument and moral teaching. Its text joins material associated with both major schools of tannaitic interpretation.
prose.study: You follow the Sifre from Deuteronomy's verses to the rules and stories drawn from them.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Sifre Deuteronomy at the yeshiva.

work_seder_olam_rabbah.composer: Anonymous; traditionally attributed to Yose ben Halafta

prose.name: Seder Olam Rabbah
prose.desc: A rabbinic ordering of biblical and Second Temple time.
prose.detail: Seder Olam links the generations from Creation to the destruction of the Second Temple, compressing biblical chronology into a coherent rabbinic historical frame.
prose.study: You count generations and reigns in the Seder Olam's compressed chronology.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Seder Olam Rabbah at the yeshiva.

prose.name: Avot de-Rabbi Natan
prose.desc: An expansive companion to Pirkei Avot.
prose.detail: Two recensions preserve sayings, anecdotes and ethical expansions around the tractate Avot. It turns terse maxims about teachers and students into scenes of rabbinic life.
prose.study: You linger over an ethical saying and the stories Avot de-Rabbi Natan builds around it.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Avot de-Rabbi Natan at the yeshiva.

prose.name: Pesikta de-Rav Kahana
prose.desc: Homilies for festivals and special Sabbaths.
prose.detail: The Pesikta gathers Palestinian sermons for the festival readings, fasts and consolations after Tisha b'Av. It was a living storehouse for preaching rather than a continuous commentary.
prose.study: You read a homily shaped for the season's Torah and prophetic readings.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Pesikta de-Rav Kahana at the yeshiva.

prose.name: Leviticus Rabbah
prose.desc: A classical midrash of sermons on Leviticus.
prose.detail: Leviticus Rabbah turns the sacrificial book into Sabbath preaching: each portion opens through proverbs, parables and the ethical life of the community.
prose.study: You follow a preacher from a proverb to the opening verse of Leviticus.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Leviticus Rabbah at the yeshiva.

work_lamentations_rabbah.rank_desc: A classical midrash of mourning and consolation

prose.name: Lamentations Rabbah
prose.desc: A midrash of destruction, grief and future consolation.
prose.detail: Stories of Jerusalem's fall and the suffering of its people surround each verse of Lamentations. The book supplies a communal language for mourning without surrendering hope.
prose.study: You read a lament and the stories the rabbis set beside it.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Lamentations Rabbah at the yeshiva.

work_tanhuma.rank_desc: A widely used homiletic midrash on the Torah

prose.name: Midrash Tanhuma
prose.desc: A Torah homily collection with legal openings and parables.
prose.detail: The Tanhuma collections frame the weekly portion with a practical legal question, then move through parable and exposition. Medieval commentators, including Rashi, cited them often.
prose.study: You begin with a legal question and follow Tanhuma into the week's portion.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Midrash Tanhuma at the yeshiva.

work_targum_jonathan.rank_desc: The Aramaic Targum of the Prophets
work_targum_jonathan.composer: Anonymous; traditionally attributed to Jonathan ben Uzziel

prose.name: Targum Jonathan
prose.desc: The Aramaic interpretation of the Prophets.
prose.detail: Targum Jonathan translates the Prophets while quietly explaining difficult names, prophecies and passages. Its interpretive voice became part of the rabbinic reading of the haftarah.
prose.study: You read the prophetic verse through the Targum's Aramaic interpretation.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Targum Jonathan at the yeshiva.

prose.name: Targum Pseudo-Jonathan
prose.desc: An expansive Torah Targum filled with legend and law.
prose.detail: More than a translation, this Aramaic rendering of the Torah carries biblical names into later legend, law and angelic lore. Its attribution to Jonathan is traditional, not historical.
prose.study: You pause over the Targum's additions beside the Torah's brief words.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Targum Pseudo-Jonathan at the yeshiva.

work_sefer_yosippon.rank_desc: A medieval Hebrew history of the Second Temple

prose.name: Sefer Yosippon
prose.desc: A Hebrew history of the Second Temple and the Roman war.
prose.detail: Written in southern Italy from Josephus and late antique sources, Yosippon gave medieval Jewish readers a Hebrew account of the Hasmoneans, Herod and the destruction of the Temple.
prose.study: You read the rise and fall of the Second Temple in a Hebrew historical voice.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Sefer Yosippon at the yeshiva.

prose.name: Allegorical Treatises of Philo
prose.desc: Greek-Jewish readings of Scripture through Platonic philosophy.
prose.detail: Philo reads the Torah as an allegory of the soul and the cosmos, blending Jewish Scripture with Greek philosophy. Medieval Jewish access was limited and indirect, so this is a rare and disputable text rather than a rabbinic authority.
prose.study: You test Philo's philosophical allegory against the plain words of the Torah.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered the Allegorical Treatises of Philo at the yeshiva.

work_josephus_jewish_war.rank_desc: A Greek history of the Roman-Jewish war

prose.name: The Jewish War
prose.desc: Josephus' Greek account of the revolt against Rome.
prose.detail: Josephus narrates the revolt, civil struggle and destruction of Jerusalem as a participant and later Roman client. Medieval Jews more often met this history through Yosippon than in its Greek original.
prose.study: You weigh Josephus' close account of catastrophe and survival.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered The Jewish War at the yeshiva.

work_toldot_yeshu.composer: Anonymous; multiple Hebrew, Aramaic and Judeo-Arabic recensions

prose.name: Toldot Yeshu
prose.desc: A contested polemical counter-history of Jesus.
prose.detail: Toldot Yeshu is not a single stable book but a family of sharp, often satirical narratives transmitted in several Jewish languages. It is included as a disputed work of polemical religious thought: never an ordinary source of doctrine, but historically real and open to approval or cherem.
prose.study: You read a difficult counter-narrative whose versions differ from manuscript to manuscript.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Toldot Yeshu at the yeshiva.

prose.name: Agron of David al-Fasi
prose.desc: A major Karaite Hebrew-Arabic biblical lexicon.
prose.detail: David al-Fasi collected Hebrew roots and their Arabic meanings to make Scripture yield its grammar and vocabulary. Later Karaites used the Agron as a foundational tool of exact biblical interpretation.
prose.study: You work from a Hebrew root through David al-Fasi's Arabic glosses.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered the Agron at the yeshiva.

prose.name: Commentary of Salmon ben Jeroham
prose.desc: A Karaite reading of Psalms, Lamentations and Ecclesiastes.
prose.detail: Salmon's Arabic commentaries apply the Karaite demand for scriptural proof to the Writings, while arguing fiercely with rabbinic tradition. They belong to the ninth- and tenth-century flowering of Karaite letters.
prose.study: You follow Salmon's close reading of a verse and his challenge to rabbinic interpretation.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered the Commentary of Salmon ben Jeroham at the yeshiva.

work_levi_ben_yefet_mitzvot.rank_desc: A Karaite compendium of the commandments

prose.name: Sefer ha-Mitzvot of Levi ben Yefet
prose.desc: A Karaite legal compendium grounded in Scripture.
prose.detail: Levi ben Yefet's Arabic work on the commandments was used by later Karaite codifiers. It records both differences with the rabbis and arguments within the Karaite movement itself.
prose.study: You trace a commandment from verse to Levi ben Yefet's reasoning.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Sefer ha-Mitzvot of Levi ben Yefet at the yeshiva.

work_samaritan_pentateuch.rank_desc: The Samaritan Torah of Mount Gerizim

prose.name: Samaritan Pentateuch
prose.desc: The Torah received by the Samaritan community.
prose.detail: The Samaritan Pentateuch shares the five books of Moses with a distinct textual tradition and a theology centred on Mount Gerizim. It is Divine Scripture for Samaritans, and a rare, contested witness for other Jews.
prose.study: You compare the Samaritan Torah's reading with the familiar Hebrew text.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered the Samaritan Pentateuch at the yeshiva.

prose.name: Samaritan Targum
prose.desc: An Aramaic translation of the Samaritan Torah.
prose.detail: The Samaritan Targum brings the community's Hebrew Torah into its Aramaic speech, often retaining readings that differ from rabbinic Targumim.
prose.study: You read the Samaritan Torah through its Aramaic rendering.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered the Samaritan Targum at the yeshiva.

prose.name: Memar Marqah
prose.desc: The theological sayings of the Samaritan sage Marqah.
prose.detail: Marqah's Memar joins exposition of the Torah with teaching on Moses, creation, repentance and the final restoration. Samaritans remembered him as their greatest early author.
prose.study: You read Marqah's compressed theology of Moses and the world.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Memar Marqah at the yeshiva.

work_defter.composer: Marqah, Amram Darah and later Samaritan poets

prose.name: Defter
prose.desc: A Samaritan collection of prayers and hymns.
prose.detail: The Defter preserves the core of Samaritan worship: prayers, alphabetic hymns and services for the sacred calendar. Its oldest layers are associated with Marqah and his circle, while the book continued to grow.
prose.study: You follow the Defter's hymn through its ordered letters and recurring prayer.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered the Defter at the yeshiva.

work_orit.rank_desc: The Ge'ez scriptural corpus of the Beta Israel

prose.name: Orit
prose.desc: The Ge'ez Torah of the Beta Israel.
prose.detail: Orit is the Beta Israel's inherited scriptural Torah, read in Ge'ez and bound to a tradition distinct from rabbinic Talmudic learning. It is Divine Scripture for Haymanot, not a Rabbanite volume in translation.
prose.study: You chant the Orit's Ge'ez Torah slowly, attending to its inherited wording.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered the Orit at the yeshiva.

work_teezaza_sanbat.rank_desc: A Beta Israel book of Sabbath commandments

prose.name: Te'ezaza Sanbat
prose.desc: The Commandments of the Sabbath in the Beta Israel canon.
prose.detail: Te'ezaza Sanbat gathers a distinctive Ethiopian Jewish vision of Sabbath observance in Ge'ez. Its surviving textual history is difficult to date precisely, so its medieval date is deliberately approximate.
prose.study: You work through the Sabbath's commands as the Beta Israel received them.
prose.yeshiva_msg: has mastered Te'ezaza Sanbat at the yeshiva.

work_cochin_copper_plates.rank_desc: A South Indian Jewish community charter
work_cochin_copper_plates.composer: The ruler of Kerala's Jewish charter tradition

prose.name: Copper Plates of Joseph Rabban
prose.desc: A royal charter remembered by the Jews of Kerala.
prose.detail: The Cochin Jewish tradition preserved copper plates granting Joseph Rabban and his descendants communal rights on the Malabar coast. This is a charter and a memory of diaspora belonging, not an invented Indian Talmud or philosophical school.
prose.study: You decipher a local royal grant and the place it gives a Jewish community in Kerala.
